title: Load Orbit experimentation notes: occupancy priming & repeatability
body:
Purpose:
This is a lab journal for an experimental throughput harness I prototyped to (a) reduce run-to-run variance, (b) explicitly surface occupancy drift over long runs, and (c) test different warmup/priming schemas that avoid false positive flaky regressions.

Why a new approach?
We have many bakebooks that focus on warmup and deterministic seeds; however, I wanted a lightweight, repeatable harness that: uses cohort-based priming (mix of synthetic prefixes + short real traces), measures occupancy as a first-class signal (not just QPS), and enforces thermal-aware pacing when GPU temperature or clock throttling is observed. Think of the test as "orbit": we launch a seed distribution into model runtime, observe orbital stability (occupancy vs time), and only capture steady-state when the orbit is tight.

High-level principles:
- Occupancy-first: capture per-GPU occupancy (KV cache memory, active thread occupancy, cuBLAS utilization) as primary stability metric. Throughput follows occupancy.
- Seed hygiene: run multiple fixed RNG seeds per experiment (3–5) but also include a canonical golden-seed trace set for regression detection.
- Epoched warmup: instead of one continuous warmup window, run 3 short warmup epochs (30s, 60s, 120s) with increasing target QPS to avoid large thermal spikes that destabilize kernels.
- Thermal shadowing: sample GPU temp and clock every 5s; if temp rise > 6C during warmup, reduce next epoch target by 20%.
- Repeatability gates: only mark a run valid if occupancy variance across seeds < 6% and tail latency CV < 8%.

Load generator config (example snippets used in runs)
- arrival pattern: poisson (lambda = target_qps) with jitter factor 0.12
- seq length distribution: mix [8:0.5, 64:0.3, 256:0.15, 1024:0.05] (token counts)
- concurrency target: derived from target_qps * avg_latency_ms / 1000 and clamped to GPU batch capacity
- rng seeds: [1729, 2027, 4096, 8191] (rotate per-subrun)

Sample loadgen command (lab shorthand):
loadgen run --profile orbit --target-qps 180 --arrival poisson --seq-dist "8:0.5,64:0.3,256:0.15,1024:0.05" --rng-seed 1729 --cohort-size 16 --log-occupancy /tmp/orbit-1729.json

Warmup/priming schedule (epoched)
- epoch 0 (primer): 30s at 10% QPS, send short real-prefix cache hits (from golden trace) to populate KV cache quickly.
- epoch 1 (ramp): 60s at 35% QPS, randomize prompt lengths to activate different kernel paths.
- epoch 2 (stress ramp): 120s at 80% QPS, observe thermal and occupancy settling.
- settle window: 60s passive observation (no capture) to allow pacing to stabilize.
- capture window: 5 minutes of telemetry for metricsaggregation.

Occupancy signals we capture (how I instrumented)
- KV cache occupancy (items and bytes) per model shard
- GPU memory used / free (reserving a 2–3% headroom margin)
- cuBLAS/cuDNN SM utilization and active warps
- kernel launch latency histogram (microprofile)
- blocking queue depth on runtime input queue
- per-request tokenization and response token counts
- host->device memcpy bandwidth and stalls

Stability/validity rules (automated)
1) During capture window, compute sliding 30s window of occupancy; steady-state if max-min <= 6% for at least 180s.
2) Latency P95 drift between seeds <= 10% and overall CV <= 8%.
3) No GPU thermal events (clock downshift or ECC warnings) in capture window. If event observed, throw away run and mark as thermal-failure.

Metrics to publish for each run (CSV row per run)
- run_id, model, quantization, hardware, target_qps, epoch_plan, rng_seeds_used (comma), occupancy_mean, occupancy_std, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cpu_load, gpu_util_pct_mean, mem_used_mb, failures_flag, notes

Temporal/long-run checks
- Drift sweep: run 6 back-to-back captures (each 5m) over 2 hours to measure occupancy decay or growth. Useful to detect slow memory leaks or KV eviction effects.
- Thermal bench: run same workload at 30%, 60%, 90% QPS but keep epoch schedule identical to observe how different ramping affects final occupancy.

Examples of observed failures (notes from runs)
- Run 2025-12-05: high occupancy but P95 spiked at minute 7 — root cause was thread oversubscription on the host (worker threads > cores) which raised memcpy stalls. Remedied by lowering client pipeline depth.
- Run 2026-01-09: occupancy slowly dropped over 40m — KV cache thrash due to badly aligned prefix batching; fixed by switching to cohort-aligned batching (group similar prefixes into same batch).

Checklist for a reproducible experiment (to-do before capturing baseline)
- [ ] pin model version and commit id in metadata
- [ ] snapshot GPU driver and cuda/cuDNN versions
- [ ] set host CPU governor to performance (documented in run notes)
- [ ] ensure network topology stable (no major flows on host NICs)
- [ ] run 2 short smoke runs to validate arrival pattern generator
- [ ] collect golden-seed trace tarball and store in S3/ARTIFACTS with run_id

Automation notes (how harness orchestrates runs)
- Orchestrator schedules seed-rotations automatically: for each RNG seed, run full epoch schedule and capture. After all seeds complete, apply repeatability gates.
- If thermal-failure observed, orchestrator retries once with epoch targets reduced by 25% and logs additional diagnostics.
- Results are pushed to a central CSV and small LT (long-term) JSON summary that contains only meta fields (run_id, outcome, tags) for quick dashboards.

Open questions / TODOs
- Is the 6% occupancy variance gate too strict for larger multi-model fanout scenarios? need to run a parameter sweep across model counts.
- Should we adopt a canonical mini-trace of 10 prefixes per model (across customers) as the golden seed instead of RNG-only traces? pros/cons: realism vs reproducibility.
- Explore adaptive warmup: instead of fixed epochs, use occupancy derivative (dOccupancy/dt) < threshold to advance. Might be more robust but adds nondeterminism to schedule length.

Notes to self (informal)
- Name: Load Orbit because the occupancy curve looks like orbital eccentricity plots.
- Keep this doc light — capture new run logs in /runs/orbit/<date>/ and link them in Confluence if a pattern emerges.
- Talk to SRE about adding a low-overhead occupancy exporter (in runtime) rather than relying on eBPF probes.

Appendix: sample CSV header I push to S3 for aggregation
run_id,model,model_commit,hw,quant,target_qps,rng_seeds,epoch_plan,occupancy_mean,occupancy_std,p50_ms,p95_ms,capture_duration_s,thermal_flag,notes

End of note.

Unresolved: whether we should commit this harness to the main loadbench repo as 'orbit' or keep it an internal lab experiment for a quarter.
